authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: Observed behavior showed elevated DDoS-to-Benign predictions in the plain attack branch and a lower rate in the defended branch. Reconstruction attribution distance decreased toward the paired preattack reference, subject to stated limitations.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.343306 versus 0.077628 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.080254, an absolute reduction of 0.263053 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.000000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.837453 to 0.306140, with recovery fraction 0.634439.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but it does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Malicious intent is unsupported and is not asserted.
Oracle clean recovery is unsupported and is not asserted.
No client flagging, threshold, trust-weight, reconstruction, or aggregation decision is made.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator was the paired round 4 preattack reference rather than an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle clean attribution states were unavailable and were not substituted.
Per-client detector scores and numeric threshold values were not present in the selected summary artifacts.
The evidence is development and validation evidence; reserved test arrays remained closed.
